newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam to slash cost of international phone calls.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam to slash cost of international phone calls.

text.p: Vietnam will cut the cost of international telephone calls by between 5.02 and 23.46 percent from January 1, official media reports said on Friday.
The reports said the tariff reduction, Vietnam Post and Telecommunication Corporation's (VNPT) sixth since 1991 and its first in over two years, would save customers over $16 million in 1997.
VNPT will also offer customers a tariff discount of 15 percent for calls made at night on Sundays and on public holidays.

Foreign companies and individuals in Vietnam frequently complain about the high cost of placing a call outside the country. The first minute of a call to the United States from Vietnam is $3.90 and each additional minute costs $3. Calling Vietnam from the United States costs just $1.82 a minute.
A recent study by VNPT showed that incoming calls from abroad, measured in minutes, grew 6.5 times faster than outgoing international calls from 1991 to 1995.

"The main reason for such a situation is that international telephone charge rates set by the VNPT are pretty high not only by Vietnamese income standards but also higher than those charged by international telecommunications companies," the Vietnam Economic Times said in a recent report.
